To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the performance of the pPPD is better than that of the EPD and PPD, (b) the performance of EPD and PDD is better than that for homogeneous traffic sources, (c) the performance of pPPD is similar to that of EPD and pPPD for heterogeneous traffic sources, (d) the performance of heterogeneous traffic sources is better than that with homogeneous sources for all three packet dropping schemes.
(1) pPPD is the best policy for homogeneous sources and (2) EPD is the best for heterogeneous sources.
the application level performance of the three packet dropping policies are very different in heterogeneous environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of heterogeneous sources over heterogeneous networks under different packet dropping policies.
the performance of selective packet dropping schemes under heterogeneous traffic and heterogeneous network environments.
the performance analysis of selective packet dropping schemes under heterogeneous traffic sources and heterogeneous networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of pPPD is the best, and EPD is the worst, in terms of packet delay and packet loss.
the performance of the selective packet dropping schemes is very sensitive to the traffic mix.
the performance of pPPD is better than PPD and EPD in terms of application layer performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in heterogeneous networks the performance is not only dependent on the traffic source but also on the packet dropping scheme and the network topology.
in a heterogeneous environment, PPD performs better than EPD, and pPPD performs better than PPD.
in general pPPD performs better than EPD and PPD, especially when the number of nodes in the network is large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of selective packet dropping depends on the type of traffic and the network environment.
the pPPD scheme is the most effective in reducing end-to-end delay and jitter while maintaining the highest level of throughput.
the packet dropping scheme that performs the best under a given set of conditions is not the same for all conditions.
